title: UiSessionSnapshot
description: Everything a client needs to render a session's header and transcript.

active_background_tasks.description: Registry-backed background processes still active for this session. Additive/defaulted so older runtimes decode as no known live process.

active_tools.description: Live render state needed to reconnect while a long turn is still running. All fields are additive/defaulted for protocol compatibility.

available_models.description: Models the user can switch to (for the model picker, ).

background_tasks.description: Every background task the durable log knows for this session, including the ones the live registry no longer holds. A task that vanished with a crashed runtime appears as `lost`, never as completed and never as a silently dropped record. Additive: an older runtime reports none.

branch.description: VCS branch, if the repository is a git repo.

children.description: Every delegated child of this session, oldest first, from durable storage.

collaboration.description: Product collaboration axis (`chat | plan | goal`). The runtime routes submissions and applies the read-only planning overlay from this value.

execution_task.description: A durable task committed from a Chat turn that still owes work. Additive: absent when no goal is running. The session's collaboration axis says the interaction mode, not whether work is owed.

finalization_stage.description: Typed in-flight terminalization stage. Present only while the runtime still owns an active turn after the final assistant message.

foreign_origin.description: Where this session came from when it was created by importing another agent's session. Additive: absent on an ordinary native session and on runtimes that predate import.

interrupted_tool_calls.description: Tool calls whose outcome a crash left unknown. Non-empty means the next turn is blocked behind the crash-recovery gate until the user acknowledges it; nothing is replayed by that acknowledgement. Additive: an older runtime reports none.

last_sequence.description: The event-log sequence this snapshot reflects — the resync anchor. A client that fell behind (broadcast lag, reconnect) takes a fresh snapshot and resumes the event stream *after* this sequence, so it neither double-applies nor misses a canonical event. `None` when unknown (e.g. a brand-new session with no events yet).

latest_turn_ordinal.description: Ordinal of the newest durable turn in this session. A client that submitted work and later correlates its terminal compares this value: the projected terminal always belongs to the newest turn, so an ordinal that moved on means a different turn now owns the terminal. Additive: an older runtime reports `None`.

recaps.description: Durable goal recaps for this session's goals (long-goal P3), oldest first. Each maps to one persisted GoalCheckpoint; a reopened client interleaves them into history by `transcript_ordinal`. Additive.

thinking.description: Runtime-projected Thinking Level state, in the user's own vocabulary. Absent on old runtimes so a new client keeps its boot-time value; a present value with `access: unsupported` means the model cannot be asked, which the client says rather than inventing a level.

user_shells.description: User shell executions: the active one (if any) plus a bounded recent history, newest last. Additive/defaulted like the rest of this block.

vision.description: Whether the current model accepts image input (spec §42).

work_profile.description: Deprecated compatibility field. New runtimes emit `single`; historical values never control tool exposure. Clients must not display a selector.

AnswerEffect.description:
Whether a started call acts on the turn's answer.

A protocol-owned DTO: the runtime decides this once (in its client projection, via the tool vocabulary) and every surface reads the stamped value instead of re-classifying the tool name. Four renderers each guessing is what made `FinalAnswer` a second truth source.

The outcome is frozen by execution presentation contract v1 (§I9) and locked by the shared fixture corpus (`testdata/execution_presentation/v1/`).

oneOf.description: Substantive work: a message before it was interim narration, not the turn's answer.
Answer-preserving bookkeeping or observation: an answer written before it survives.

ApprovalId.description: Identifies a pending permission approval request.

AttachmentId.description: Identifies a pending or sent attachment.

AttachmentRef.description: A reference to a processed, stored attachment (spec §39). Carries only metadata; the bytes are addressed by `sha256` in the media store.

sha256.description: Content-address of the processed bytes in the media store.

BuildIdentity.description: The build a binary was produced from.

dirty.description: Built from a modified working tree. Metadata about provenance, not an identity: use `fingerprint` to tell two builds apart.

fingerprint.description:
Deterministic digest of the exact source this artifact was built from (`revision` + the working-tree delta). Two runs of the SAME executable share it, so a dirty development build recognises itself instead of being retired on every launch; a rebuild from different source does not share it, so a true new build still replaces the old runtime.

Empty for a runtime built before this field existed: those fall back to the conservative `dirty` rule.

revision.description: The source revision. `unknown` when the build had no git available — which is itself a mismatch against anything, by design.

read_only.description: Whether this child held a physically read-only toolset. It used to be a list of semantic capability labels; what a client needs is the structural bound.

ChildLimit.description: Which bound stopped a child whose stop is [`ChildStop::Budget`]. A mirror of the runtime's typed limit, not a second reason vocabulary: without it a client can only say "budget", which renders a wall-clock timeout and a spent token budget the same. `Duration` is the wall clock — the bound the runtime's child cap enforces.

oneOf.description: The child's own round window.
The absolute round ceiling.

ChildOutcome.description: The four-way reading of a settled child's result. "Finished with nothing to flag" and "stopped with nothing to show" are opposite facts; a client renders them from this field, never from the summary text.

ChildStop.description: How a settled child's activation ended.

ClarificationQuestionKind.description:
How one question in a clarification is answered.

The kind is explicit rather than inferred from `options` being empty: a single-choice question with no options is unanswerable, while a text question is the only shape whose answer is typed. A client that guessed would silently turn a missing option list into a free-text prompt.

oneOf.description: Exactly one option (or a free-text answer when `allow_other` is set).
Zero or more options.
A free-text answer.

CommandId.description: Identifies a client command, used as an idempotency key: a command may be delivered more than once (at-least-once), so the same id must not run the action twice.

CompactionRecord.description: One recorded compaction fold: the estimated transcript size before and after. The runtime records this at the fold boundary, not the TUI.

ContextAccounting.description: What one assembled model request is made of.

compact_at_tokens.description: The SOFT fold threshold: where compaction is expected and may be abandoned. It is strictly below [`Self::input_capacity_tokens`] whenever both are known, because a percentage policy reserves the completion first and takes its share of what is left.

context_window_tokens.description: The model's declared context window (an exact declared fact), when known.

fold_state.description: The exact decision for THIS request, from the one classifier the harness folds with. A display may not re-derive it from a rounded percentage.

free_tokens.description: `context_window - used` when the window is known.

headroom_tokens.description: Extra safety margin on top of the completion reservation.

input_capacity_tokens.description: The EFFECTIVE INPUT CAPACITY: `window − reservation − headroom`, when a window is declared and leaves input room. This — never the whole model window — is the denominator of compaction utilization, and it is the same number [`Self::fold_state`] compares against.

last_compaction.description: Most recent compaction fold, when one has run.

output_reservation_tokens.description: The completion this harness reserves per request.

reasoning_projection.description: What the request projection did with the requested reasoning-retention arm: which turns carried reasoning, and how many the route contract had to keep against the request. Present on every snapshot computed from a projection, so an overridden treatment is visible rather than assumed.

used_tokens.description: Estimated input tokens of this request — the sum of the top-level categories, by construction.

ContextCategory.description: One mutually exclusive slice of the request. `children` holds the next level of drill-down when the runtime can reliably separate it; a category with no reliable sub-split has none.

calls.description: Tool invocations counted in this slice (nonzero only for tool leaves and `tool_calls`).

children.description: Next drill-down level, when one exists.

name.description: Stable key (`messages`, `system`, `tool_definitions`, `user`, … or a tool name for a per-tool leaf). The UI may localize by `name`; it must never parse `label`.

tokens.description: Estimated tokens in this slice. Summing the top level equals [`ContextAccounting::used_tokens`] by construction.

ContextPressure.description: Deterministic context-pressure level derived from real thresholds — never a model's judgement.

ConversationStateOwnership.description:
Who owns the conversation state a provider validates against.

Today every supported route is [`Self::ClientManaged`]: the harness resends the full active history. The vocabulary exists so a future route that keeps the state server-side (`previous_response_id`-style) can say so without the kernel assuming client-owned replay state is an eternal property of models.

oneOf.description: The client resends the model-visible history on every request.
The provider keeps the conversation state; the client sends a cursor. No supported route constructs this yet.

FailureCategory.description: What kind of failure this is, in product terms. Vendor error codes are not part of this vocabulary — `Moonshot invalid_request_error`, `OpenAI invalid_request_error` and `Anthropic invalid_request_error` are all just [`FailureCategory::InvalidRequest`] here.

oneOf.description: A network/transport failure reaching a provider or service.
A timeout elapsed.
Authentication or authorization failed.
A rate limit was hit.
The provider itself is unavailable or failed.
The request was malformed or rejected as invalid.

A local provider/model configuration or resolution failure: the request was never sent because this process could not build a route for it. Distinct from [`FailureCategory::InvalidRequest`] so a client never reports a local misconfiguration as a provider rejection.
A tool or command failed.
A runtime/infrastructure failure that is not a provider call.
Permission was refused.
The work was cancelled.
Anything not covered above.

FailureDelivery.description: What the transport could prove about whether the request reached the provider. Mirrors `leveler_model::DeliveryState` in product terms.

oneOf.description: Provably never sent.
Written, but no response was observed.
A complete HTTP status was returned.
The response stream began and ended early. `text`/`tool_args` are what it produced before the cut.

text.description: Assistant text arrived before the cut.

tool_args.description: Tool-call arguments began arriving before the cut.

oneOf.description: Delivery could not be established.

FailureRetryability.description: Whether an automatic retry is possible, from the delivery truth. Mirrors `leveler_model::Retryability` in product terms.

oneOf.description: The request provably did no provider-side work, or the provider asked to be retried: a bounded automatic retry is safe.
The request may have reached the provider: retrying could duplicate work, so it is never automatic.
Delivery could not be established: never automatic, reported as unknown.
Retrying the identical request cannot help.

FailureSource.description: Which boundary produced the failure. Sources share retry primitives but never share error truth: a provider disconnect, an MCP disconnect, a failed `curl` command and a runtime-IPC drop are different facts.

oneOf.description: The model provider transport.
The runtime itself (persistence, lifecycle, IPC).
An MCP server transport.
A tool or command's own network/execution.
Local execution that did not touch the network.

FinalizationStage.description:
The mechanical work still running after the assistant has produced its final response but before the runtime publishes the task terminal.

This is lifecycle chrome, not a second completion authority: the terminal event remains the only fact that ends the turn.

oneOf.description: Wait for work already admitted by the turn to settle.
Run a completion review explicitly required by the task contract.
Resolve the task outcome from the collected facts.
Commit and publish the canonical terminal fact.

FoldRequirement.description:
What a measured request's pressure means for the context fold, and therefore what a failed briefing costs the turn.

The fold has TWO bounds, and they answer different questions. The quality threshold is where recall is expected to degrade — folding there is a quality choice that may be abandoned. The hard capacity is where a request can no longer legally be sent — folding there is REQUIRED, and a fold that cannot be produced must still be brought under capacity mechanically or the turn fails explicitly.

This is the ONE contract every active-context entry shares: coding/drive, chat, resume and the accounting that REPORTS which state a request is in. Entries provide the measured facts (projected tokens, resolved bounds); this decides what a failure means — and, because the display reads this same function, a shown trigger state can never disagree with the decision.

It lives beside the threshold arithmetic ([`ModelLimits`]) rather than in a harness: the classification is a comparison of three numbers and every consumer must read the same implementation.

oneOf.description: At or below the quality boundary: nothing to fold.
Over the quality boundary but within hard capacity. Sending the request uncompacted is legal, so a failed briefing keeps the original active history and the turn continues.
Over the hard capacity. Without a fold the request cannot legally be sent, so a failed briefing must be folded mechanically or the turn fails without ever sending an oversized request.

MessageId.description:
Identifies a single assistant/user message in the transcript.

A protocol-level id (the runtime persists messages as an ordered log, not by id); it lets streaming deltas target the right in-flight message.

MissingReasoningReplay.description:
What a replayed assistant turn carries when it captured no reasoning.

Orthogonal to [`ReasoningReplayScope`]: "should reasoning be replayed?" and "what does an empty turn carry?" are different requirements, and providers differ on each of them independently.

oneOf.description: Send nothing. A turn that produced no reasoning carries no field.

Send the empty string. Some endpoints validate the key's presence on a replayed assistant turn independently of what the turn captured (measured: DeepSeek rejects a tool-bearing history whose assistant turn omits the key, and accepts an empty value on a turn that captured none).

ModelRef.description: A provider + model pair. The rest of the system routes on this, never on a bare model-name string.

NativeContextCapabilities.description:
Provider-native context management the route exposes.

All fields are `false` for every route supported today: CodeLeveler owns the active-history lifecycle. They are declared (not derived) so a future route can advertise e.g. server-side reasoning pruning without the harness having to branch on its name — the context policy reads these flags. A flag that no route declares is simply not consulted.

native_compaction.description: The provider performs its own history compaction.

reasoning_pruning.description: The provider can prune historical reasoning server-side.

server_state.description: The provider owns conversation state across requests.

ObservationClass.description: Presentation class for a meaningful durable event. Unknown tools map to [`Self::Tool`].

PlanStepStatus.description: The lifecycle state of a plan step (mirrors the orchestrator's `NodeStatus`).

oneOf.description:
The model removed this step from its own plan while it was still open.

Not delivered (so it never counts toward a completed plan) and not open work the runtime should keep driving. Keeping it distinct from `Skipped` is what stops a removed step from being projected as a legitimate completion.

ReasoningIntegrity.description:
How the route requires retained reasoning to be preserved.

Orthogonal to representation: a route may never carry reasoning, carry it as an editable field, or carry it as an opaque block — and separately it either accepts a harness decision to fold/drop a retained turn, or it does not. This is the dimension the context lifecycle consults when it asks "may I cut this boundary?": it never asks "is this model DeepSeek?".

oneOf.description: The route puts no integrity requirement on reasoning it retains.

Every assistant turn still in the active history must replay its captured reasoning verbatim. The harness may not truncate, rewrite or silently omit it while the turn remains; only the context lifecycle may remove the whole turn.

ReasoningProjectionSummary.description:
What the projection did with the requested retention arm, in facts rather than in a claim.

An experiment that asked for `None` and got every retained turn's reasoning anyway must not be recorded as `None`: [`Self::protocol_protected_turns`] is exactly how many turns the provider contract kept that the requested arm would have dropped.

captured_turns.description: Assistant turns in the request that captured reasoning.

carried_turns.description: Of those, how many carry the channel on the wire.

contract.description: The route contract the projection ran under.

empty_turns.description: Assistant turns THIS route produced that captured no reasoning. The provider completed the turn and returned no thinking, which is a fact about the turn, not a gap in the record.

foreign_turns.description: Assistant turns another route produced. Their reasoning is private to the model that wrote it, so it is never carried to this one: the turn's text, tool calls and tool results stay, its thinking does not. Counted rather than silently dropped.

protocol_protected_turns.description: Turns the requested arm would have dropped but the provider contract requires. A route that replays captured reasoning requires the full reasoning of every retained assistant turn, so this is the arm's difference from `All`. Non-zero ⇒ the requested treatment was NOT fully applied, and the request's reasoning cost cannot be reduced by the arm: the lever is the context lifecycle, which removes whole turns.

unknown_provenance_turns.description: Assistant turns whose producing route was not recorded (a payload written before provenance existed, or a request assembled by a runtime that cannot report its route). Not the same fact as [`Self::empty_turns`]: "nobody said" is not "the model produced none".

unproven_reasoning_turns.description: Of the unproven turns, how many captured reasoning that was therefore withheld from the request. The channel is not replayed (nothing proves it belongs to this route), but the turn's text, tool calls and tool results stay, and a route that requires the key's presence still gets its legal empty value. Reported so a reader can tell this from a route that genuinely measured no reasoning.

ReasoningReplayContract.description:
The resolved reasoning contract for one route.

Four orthogonal dimensions, none of which is a model or provider name:

* [`Self::representation`] — the form captured reasoning takes on the wire; * [`Self::scope`] / [`Self::missing`] — when it is carried, and what an empty replayed turn carries; * [`Self::integrity`] — whether retained reasoning may be changed; * [`Self::state`] / [`Self::native_context`] — who owns the validated state, and what context management the provider offers.

The context lifecycle reads this contract to decide whether a cut boundary keeps the protocol valid. A provider never gets a branch of its own.

integrity.description: Whether retained reasoning must be replayed verbatim.

missing.description: What an empty replayed turn carries.

representation.description: The form captured reasoning takes when replayed.

state.description: Who owns the validated conversation state.

ReasoningReplayScope.description:
When captured reasoning is carried back to a provider on historical assistant turns.

This is a ROUTE fact, not a harness preference: it is resolved from the protocol the route speaks and the route's declared compatibility. A provider that validates the field and a provider that has no field at all both have to be expressible without naming either of them.

oneOf.description: The route has no channel for historical reasoning. Captured reasoning stays in the durable transcript and never reaches this provider.
Carried only on requests that expose tools — the scope a provider that validates reasoning on tool rounds defines its requirement in.
Carried on every request that spans the history.

ReasoningRepresentation.description:
The FORM in which a route replays captured reasoning to the provider.

One orthogonal dimension of [`ReasoningReplayContract`]. It answers "what does the provider expect this evidence to look like?", which is a different question from [`ReasoningReplayScope`]'s "when is it carried?" and from [`ReasoningIntegrity`]'s "may we change it?".

oneOf.description:
The route has no channel for captured reasoning.

This is the default: a route carries nothing until it declares otherwise, so no route inherits another's requirement.
A plain assistant message field the harness itself composes from the captured text (today: an OpenAI-Chat-compatible `reasoning_content`).
An authenticated/opaque block the provider issued on the way in and expects back verbatim (today: Messages `thinking` / `redacted_thinking`).

ReasoningRetention.description:
How much historical assistant reasoning one request carries.

This is the REQUESTED arm. The protocol-safe effective view is produced by [`crate::RequestProjection::project`], which reports any difference.

[`ReasoningRetention::All`] is the production default and is byte-identical to carrying every reasoning block.

oneOf.description: Every historical reasoning block is carried.
Only the `n` most recent reasoning-bearing assistant turns keep their reasoning; earlier ones keep text and tool calls.
No historical reasoning is carried.

RecoveryStop.description: The interrupted call a recovery stop refuses to guess about.

RuntimeEvent.description: An event flowing from the runtime to clients.

oneOf.description: The answer to [`crate::ClientCommand::ManageSchedule`]. `response` carries domain failures too; a transport failure is the only case where no answer arrives.
The runtime finished booting and is ready for commands.

The build this client's stream is connected to, observed when the stream is first established. A long-lived runtime can outlive an application update, so the client must learn at connect time whether it is talking to the build it was installed with. Like [`RuntimeEvent::RuntimeReconnected`], an unknown identity proves nothing and is never a version change.

The client's event stream dropped and was re-established.

Emitted by the local transport, never by a runtime: it states only what the client observed — that it is connected again, and to which build. Whether the user must hear that work may have stopped, or that a restart is needed to switch versions, is a presentation decision; the transport cannot know either fact.

A runtime built before [`leveler_core::BuildIdentity`] existed reports the default identity, which is UNKNOWN. Unknown is not a version change and must never be presented as one.

runtime_restarted.description: Whether the runtime PROCESS changed across the break, when both sides of it were observed: `Some(true)` a restart, `Some(false)` the same process, `None` nothing proven. A stream reset on a live runtime is `Some(false)` and cost no work.

oneOf.description: A reconnect re-established the stream but could not re-read the session. The client's view may be pre-break state; it must say so rather than present stale facts as current.

error.description: The load/snapshot failure, unformatted. Presentation owns wording.

oneOf.description: The user acknowledged this session's crash window. `closed` interrupted tool calls were marked "outcome unknown, not replayed"; zero means there was nothing left to close (a retry or a concurrent acknowledgement). This states what the runtime wrote, not that any interrupted operation succeeded.
A session was opened / its snapshot refreshed.
Session metadata changed (model/mode/branch) without touching the transcript — refresh the header only.
The runtime needs the user to approve a risky action .
A pending approval was resolved (by any connected client, or by a timeout/cancel). Clients dismiss the matching prompt so a second client never answers an approval that no longer exists.
The agent is asking the user a clarifying question (spec §35).
A pending clarification was resolved (by any client, timeout, or cancel).
An imported attachment was processed and stored (spec §39).

command_id.description: Original delivery identity; absent for legacy raw-send imports.

oneOf.description: Importing an attachment failed.
A user message was appended to the transcript.

The runtime accepted a mid-turn input and made it durable, but no model round has received it yet.

This is the ACK boundary: unlike [`Self::UserMessageAdded`], it does not claim a transcript row exists. Every connected client paints the same row from this event, not from the submitting client's optimism.

A previously admitted input reached a terminal state.

`Delivered` means its transcript row is durable (and `ordinal` locates it); `Cancelled` means it never will be. A cancelled input is never resurrected by a later turn.
A new assistant message began; deltas will target this id.
A retry attempt began. Remove the prior transient message, if present, and clear its reasoning before applying new deltas.
A chunk of assistant text for an in-flight message.
A chunk of model reasoning/summary, rendered separately from the answer.
A model reasoning segment began. Presentation opens ONE mutable reasoning block on this; it must not append a new transcript item.

The current reasoning segment ended cleanly. `elapsed_ms` is the runtime's own measurement of the segment. Presentation freezes its mutable block into an immutable history item on this. A segment that never receives this was interrupted, not completed.
The assistant message is complete.

The runtime named the text it accepted as this turn's delivery.

The text is already on screen as an assistant message. This event does not append another copy. It tells the client which existing block is the answer, so a later progress note cannot take that place when the turn ends. `text` is the runtime's published delivery, compared by exact trimmed equality — not a guess about length or wording.
The assistant has produced its final response, while the runtime is still settling the task before its one authoritative terminal event.
Coarse progress label from the runtime, shown in the status line.
Heartbeat while a long command tool runs (runtime observability). Lets a client show "运行 cargo test" with a live elapsed instead of a bare "等待模型". Structured so TUI/Web/logs can consume it uniformly.

A model round is about to retry the same request (transient). Belongs in ephemeral status, NOT the transcript: a brief network blip must not spam the conversation. `attempt` is 1-based (the retry about to happen) and `max_attempts` the retry budget; once `attempt == max_attempts` fails the turn is surfaced, not hidden behind an unbounded wait.
Project behavior constraints loaded for this turn. Sources are workspace-relative paths; instruction contents never enter UI chrome.
A tool call started .

answer_effect.description:
Whether this call acts on the turn's answer — the runtime's own classification, stated once so no surface re-derives it from the tool name. A peer that omits it is read as [`AnswerEffect::unstated`].

[`AnswerEffect::unstated`]: crate::AnswerEffect::unstated

model_step.description: The 1-based model step whose response requested this call — the real execution-round boundary. Every call from one model response carries the same value, so a UI groups one response's calls together even when the round produced no visible assistant prose. Legacy events omit it; a client must then fall back to its old grouping rather than invent a boundary.

parallel.description: True when this call ran in the concurrent read-only batch; a UI can group such calls as one parallel burst.

oneOf.description: An admitted tool reached an actual dispatch boundary. Announcement and approval wait time are not execution time.
A tool call finished. `preview` is the runtime's truncated output; `duration_ms` is measured client-side.

applied_diff.description:
Canonical unified diff of what an edit ACTUALLY changed, with the line numbers it landed on, produced by the tool that made it.

A UI renders an edit from THIS, not from the call's arguments: an `apply_patch` hunk is located by content and `replace` matches a substring, so the request never says where the change went. `None` for every non-edit call, and for an edit whose location could not be established — the UI must then show no line numbers rather than invent one.

exit_code.description: Exit code of the process a command call ran, when it exited.

stop.description: Present only when the call was stopped: whether the runtime confirmed its whole process tree gone. A client shows "stopped" for `confirmed` alone; `unconfirmed` is an unknown outcome.

oneOf.description: Live output from a running command tool call. `stream` is `stdout` or `stderr`; `chunk` is one or more whole, sanitized lines. Transient: clients keep a bounded buffer and the completed preview is the record.
The execution plan was created or a step's status changed (spec §20).

call_id.description: The tool call that carried the declaration; absent on a resume seed and on legacy events. Clients use it to label the matching row.

created.description: True when the declaration created the plan, false when it replaced an existing one. Legacy events omit it and decode as an update, which is the only presentation their runtime ever had.

oneOf.description: The working-tree diff changed or was explicitly requested (spec §21).

query_id.description: Present only for a `RequestDiff` response. `None` is an authoritative state-change broadcast and is accepted by all clients.

oneOf.description: A requested working-tree diff could not be computed. Distinct from `DiffUpdated` with zero files, which is a real "no changes" answer: clients must never present an unreadable workspace as clean.

message.description: Machine-facing detail (git's own message or the reason the path is not a work tree). Clients own the localized label.

query_id.description: Present only for a `RequestDiff` response. `None` when the failure happened during a broadcast refresh.

oneOf.description: A conversation checkpoint was created (spec §68).
The list of stored sessions (spec §52).
The locally discovered sessions of another coding agent, newest first. `error` is present only when discovery itself could not run; an empty `sessions` list with no error is a real "nothing found".
A foreign session was imported. `session_id` is the NEW native CodeLeveler session; the source identity is carried so the client can keep it visible after the view switches.

warning.description: A source/current-workspace mismatch the person should see before trusting the continuation. Absent when the directories agree.

oneOf.description: A foreign session could not be imported. Nothing was created, and the source file was not modified.
Context package info from an orchestrated run (spec §53).
The runtime folded conversation history: `from` transcript messages became `to`. A stable product fact — clients own the wording and the locale; the runtime does not send prose for this.
Replay-only. The adaptive-context ladder that climbed the fold threshold was deleted; the variant survives so an old event log still decodes, and nothing emits one. Token budgets, not message counts.
A user shell execution (`!command`) started. User-originated direct host execution — not an agent tool call; clients render it as its own block and never feed it to the model conversation.

The same user shell execution moved from the foreground to the background. It is one process and one execution id; `task_id` links it to the background task list. Additive; older clients keep showing the foreground record until it exits.
Live output from a running user shell. `stream` is `stdout` or `stderr`. Transient: clients keep a bounded buffer; the runtime does not persist chunks.

The runtime's authoritative retained view of a user shell's output. It REPLACES the client's accumulated live chunks: the bounded live channel may have dropped bytes, so appending would preserve a hole. Emitted before the terminal event when the live view could be lossy (and always when a background execution finishes).

The exact on-disk capture of a user shell execution is complete. `directory` holds `stdout.log`, `stderr.log` and `combined.log`. Clients use it for "Copy Output"; it is never inferred from painted text. Emitted before the terminal event, and only when every stream's sidecar reports a finished copy — an unfinished capture is never advertised.
A user shell execution ended. `status` is `success | failed | cancelled`; `exit_code` is `None` when the process was killed or never spawned.

Real token usage reported by the model for the latest request. The context gauge tracks how full the window is; `input_tokens` already includes the whole prompt (system + history + tools), so the window in use is `input_tokens + output_tokens`.

A SNAPSHOT of the request that just reported, not a delta: a provider may emit it several times while one request streams, and the consumer must replace rather than add. Turn-level accounting is settled once by [`RuntimeEvent::TurnUsage`].

cached_input_tokens.description: Subset of `input_tokens` the provider served from its prefix cache. Zero when the provider reports no cache stats.

reasoning_tokens.description: Subset of `output_tokens` the provider attributed to reasoning. `None` when it reported no breakdown — unreported is not a measured zero.

oneOf.description: The settled provider usage of one finished turn, aggregated from the runtime's durable model-call ledger. Arrives before the turn terminal and is replayable; a client uses it instead of summing the transient [`RuntimeEvent::TokenUsage`] snapshots.
The accounting of the exact next model request, computed by the kernel before the request is sent. Transient: nothing persists it, and a reconnecting client gets the latest through its live view.
An orchestrated run completed; carries the summary report (spec §23).

Best-effort prediction of the user's next prompt. Transient UI chrome: it is never persisted as user input and never participates in task completion. Clients may discard it when the user has started typing.
Best-effort, transient post-turn recap requested after an idle window. It is display-only and never becomes model-visible conversation.
The current turn finished successfully.

The work completed and project verification retains its own result, but a separate required completion contract produced warnings.

`unregistered_task` is a structured terminal fact, not a reading of `reason`: the turn was an answer whose `commit_task` declaration was refused, so no durable task was registered. It must never settle a Goal. Omitted on legacy events, where the old semantics apply.
The assistant naturally finished its answer, without claiming that an external task was independently verified as complete.

The turn ended at the user's own pause boundary. The goal still owes the work the user withheld authorization to continue; nothing failed and nothing is complete. Only the user's own continuation releases it.
The turn stopped at an output limit even after bounded continuation.
The executor stopped cleanly but did not reach a successful terminal state (for example, budget exhaustion or an unresolved goal).

The goal stopped because the model declared it blocked.

This is a distinct terminal, not a flavour of [`Self::TurnIncomplete`]: the goal is NOT settled, the work already delivered stays real, and the user can continue it. `reason` is the model's own declared blocking summary; it is display-only and never decides the lifecycle — the durable `TaskFinished.stop` is the authority.

The current turn failed.

`error` is the legacy display string, kept for compatibility with older clients (CLI, Web). New presentations must prefer `failure` and must never parse `error` to decide a category, a retry, or a delivery truth.

failure.description: Structured product failure. `None` on legacy events and on failures the runtime could not type; readers fall back to `error`.

recovery.description: Present when the turn stopped because an earlier tool call was interrupted before its outcome was recorded. The runtime refuses to replay it; the client owns the wording and the next step.

oneOf.description: The current turn was cancelled (resumable).
The logical task was explicitly cancelled by the user. Terminal: unlike [`Self::TurnCancelled`] a continuation must not reopen it.
A spawned sub-agent started or finished (multi-agent delegation). One block per agent id, updated in place from running → done.

agent.description: The declarative agent it was spawned from, carried on the start. `None` for built-in role spawns, on terminals, and on events recorded before agents existed.

background.description: Whether the parent continues while this child runs. Carried on the start; `None` on a terminal, which says nothing about it.

contribution.description:
What the parent did with what this child found, once it finished.

`None` means NOT MEASURED — the runtime produced no projection — and must never be rendered as a zero. A child that reported nothing arrives as `Some` with zero counts, which is a different fact and reads differently to the user.

detail.description: The task while running; a short result summary once done.

done.description: false while running; true once the agent finished.

limit.description: Which bound fired when `stop` is `Budget`. `None` for every other stop, on the start, and for terminals recorded before it existed.

ok.description: Whether it finished successfully (only meaningful when `done`).

outcome.description: The four-way reading, once done. `None` while running and for children settled before it was recorded.

profile_id.description: Built-in capability contract this child was launched under. `None` means the runtime did not record one, not "no profile".

read_only.description: Whether this child holds a physically read-only toolset.

scope.description: Exclusive write scope fixed at spawn (empty when late-bound or read-only).

stop.description: How the activation ended, once done.

title.description: The child's short task title, carried on the start only. `None` on terminals and on children recorded before titles existed.

oneOf.description: A child's lifecycle moved without a start or a terminal: its activation died with a runtime window (`interrupted`) or a new one began under the same id (`running`). Clients update the child they already hold.
Live execution state and cumulative model usage for one spawned agent.
Live tool/step for one spawned sub-agent (attributed by `id`). Transient; older clients ignore unknown types via [`parse_runtime_event`].
Result of [`crate::ClientCommand::QueryChildContribution`]. Read-only: a snapshot of the ledger, never a mutation.

A durable goal checkpoint was cut; render it as a Recap history item (long-goal P3). Emitted for `/recap`, milestones, context compaction, and on surfacing an interruption checkpoint — the recap carries its `checkpoint_id`, so an expanded view presents the same persisted facts.
Result of [`crate::ClientCommand::ListUnfinishedGoals`]. Read-only.
Result of [`crate::ClientCommand::ListAgents`].
Result of [`crate::ClientCommand::GetAgent`]. `agent` is `None` and `error` says why when the name does not resolve.
Result of `CreateAgent` / `UpdateAgent` / `DeleteAgent`. On failure nothing was written and `error` is the reason.

agent.description: The entry as the registry now resolves it (after a create/update).

oneOf.description: A transient notification for the status line.
A background process task was started (`run_command` background=true).

pid.description: The process-group leader's OS pid, when the runtime observed one. A read-only fact for a detail view; it carries no authority. Additive; older clients ignore the unknown field.

oneOf.description: A live chunk of a background task's combined stdout/stderr, already sanitized and capped by the runtime. Additive; older clients ignore the unknown type. The final [`Self::BackgroundTaskExited`] log stays authoritative.

A still-running background task printed a readiness signal that a caller was waiting for (its own output matched an explicit pattern). `evidence` is the line that matched. This is an OBSERVATION, not a health check and not an exit: the process keeps running, and the terminal event still follows whenever it ends. Additive; older clients ignore the unknown type and keep showing the task as running.

elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds from process start to the observation.

oneOf.description: A background task's state could not be established (for example its adopted driver failed). This is not a natural exit and not a stop: the UI must show unknown, never Running, failed, or stopped.

A background task finished (exit or kill). `output` is the task's final retained log, authoritative over the streamed chunks (a lifecycle broadcast lag can drop a chunk). Empty when the runtime produced none.

stopped.description: The runtime's terminal state was `Killed`, not a natural exit: a user cancel, an agent cancel, or session cleanup stopped it. This is the authoritative distinction between "stopped" and "failed" — a stopped task is not a failure however its exit code reads. Additive; older clients ignore the unknown field.

oneOf.description: Authoritative replacement of a session's active background projection. Emitted after a lifecycle broadcast lag; history is unaffected.
Side-question (`/btw`) started; not persisted to session history.
Side-question answer chunk (often one full answer in MVP).
Side-question finished successfully.
Side-question stopped by the user before it finished. Distinct from [`Self::BtwFailed`]: the answer was interrupted, not unsuccessful, and the partial answer (if any) is what the side thread keeps.
Side-question failed.

A `/btw` side question started a read-only tool call.

The side surface has its own activity: the main turn's [`Self::ToolCallStarted`] / [`Self::ToolCallCompleted`] stay the main transcript's, and a side question never appears there. Transient and never persisted, like every other `Btw*` event.

A `/btw` side-question tool call finished.

Carries the outcome and the measured duration only — no arguments, no tool output, no error payload — because the side surface is an observer and its activity is chrome, not a record.

Coarse turn-progress / closeout signal (additive; protocol minor ≥ 1.2).

No free-form paths or tool output — safe to surface in TUI chrome and optional remote summaries. Unknown older clients that reject new variants should skip events via [`crate::event::parse_runtime_event`].

phase.description: Active | Closing | Terminal (and similar host phase labels).

oneOf.description: Result of [`crate::ClientCommand::QueryContext`]. `accounting` is `None` when no model request has been assembled yet for the session (a fresh session before its first turn).

Result of [`crate::ClientCommand::QueryObservability`]. Read-only projection of durable facts for the current or a historical session. Echoes the command's `query_id` when the peer sent one. Absent on protocol 1.5 peers — a current client must not treat that as ownership.
Result of [`crate::ClientCommand::QueryUsage`]. A projection of the runtime's durable model-call ledger for one scope. Read-only: it answers while a turn runs, and it never drives a provider request.

Result of [`crate::ClientCommand::ReloadConfig`], and the notification of an automatically applied generation. `outcome` is one of `applied` / `unchanged` / `failed`.

`version` is the generation now in force — the PREVIOUS one on a failure, because a failed reload keeps the last known good configuration. `changed` names the dimensions that moved (never their values, and never a credential). `deferred_to_next_turn` is true when a turn was already running: it keeps the generation it started with, and the next turn uses this one.

restart_required.description: Settings this generation changed that only a restart of the named component can apply. Empty means everything applied.

oneOf.description: Result of [`crate::ClientCommand::QuerySessionHistory`]: the latest turns in order. `omitted_turns` older turns were left out to bound the response; they are still in the session.

ScheduleActionWire.description: The declared work of a schedule, in wire form.

ScheduleCheck.description: One doctor check, in user language.

ScheduleGrantView.description: The persisted unattended authorization, as a user surface sees it.

requires_regrant.description: Unattended execution is not authorized right now: either no grant was ever issued, or a stored grant no longer matches the current definition. The user must authorize before the next scheduled run.

ScheduleRunView.description: One run, projected for a user surface.

ScheduleTriggerWire.description: A trigger rule in the vocabulary a user can actually choose.

oneOf.description: One RFC3339 instant.
A fixed interval in seconds, anchored at `anchor` (default now).
One local wall-clock time per day.
Local wall-clock time on selected weekdays (`mon`, `mon-fri`, ...).
Five-field cron expression.

ScheduleUsageView.description: Model usage attributed to one run. Missing totals stay missing.

ScheduleView.description: One definition with the facts a list/detail surface needs.

description.description: A one-line, user-readable statement of what runs.

revision.description: Changes whenever the definition changes; a client sends it back on update so a stale editor cannot overwrite a newer definition.

ScheduleWakeupView.description: The OS wakeup registration as observed, plus what the product can do.

interval_secs.description: The registration's wake interval, when observed.

SessionId.description: Identifies a single agent session (one user goal end to end).

ThinkingLevel.description:
How hard the user wants the model to think, in CodeLeveler's own words.

The order is the product contract: weakest → strongest, with `Auto` first because "no override" precedes explicit intensity choices.

oneOf.description: No override. CodeLeveler does not specify reasoning intensity; the provider's own default applies.
Ask the route to disable extra thinking, where it can be asked.
The strongest level this model declares — not a fixed setting.

TokenCountKind.description: How the token figures in a snapshot were produced.

oneOf.description: Every figure came from a real tokenizer.
Every figure came from the byte/char estimator.
The total is provider-reported but the breakdown is estimated.

ToolCallId.description: Identifies a tool call. Must be stable across streaming reassembly.

UiActiveBackgroundTask.description:
One background process that is still lifecycle-active in the runtime.

This is a reconnect projection, not history. Terminal tasks never appear here even though the execution registry may retain their records for `get`/`wait`.

lifetime.description: The task's lifetime (`goal`, `session`, `runtime`, `persistent`). A client exit owns only `goal`: the others survive it by contract. Additive; absent is a runtime that predates the field.

pid.description: The process-group leader's OS pid, when known. Additive; older clients decode it as absent.

ready_evidence.description: Readiness evidence observed for this still-running task, when a caller waited for a real signal in its output. Additive; absent means no signal has been observed, never that the service is not ready.

UiActiveToolCall.description: A tool invocation that was still running when a client took its snapshot.

answer_effect.description:
Whether this call acts on the turn's answer — carried so a reconnected client decides the `FinalAnswer` boundary exactly as the live one did, instead of re-classifying the tool name (see the same field on [`RuntimeEvent::ToolCallStarted`]). A snapshot from a peer that omits it is read as [`AnswerEffect::unstated`].

[`RuntimeEvent::ToolCallStarted`]: crate::RuntimeEvent::ToolCallStarted [`AnswerEffect::unstated`]: crate::AnswerEffect::unstated

elapsed_ms.description: How long the call had been running when the snapshot was taken, by the runtime's clock, so a reconnecting client does not restart it at zero.

model_step.description:
The 1-based model step whose response requested this call — the same execution-round identity [`RuntimeEvent::ToolCallStarted`] carries.

A reconnect must not re-guess the round from the tools' types or timing: the runtime already knows it, so the snapshot states it. Every call from one model response shares the value, so a reconnecting client rebuilds the same rounds it would have seen live. Legacy snapshots omit the field; a client then falls back to its old grouping rather than inventing a boundary.

[`RuntimeEvent::ToolCallStarted`]: crate::RuntimeEvent::ToolCallStarted

output_tail.description: The bounded end of the command's live output so far.

timing.description: Runtime timeline and elapsed at the snapshot boundary.

UiAgentCapability.description: The runtime capability class an agent runs under.

UiAgentDetail.description: One agent with its full definition, for an editor.

instructions.description: `None` for structural built-ins and invalid definitions.

UiAgentEntry.description: One resolvable agent name, as the registry resolves it.

description.description: The fields below are `None`/empty for an invalid definition.

harness_only.description: Launched by the harness only; a model cannot spawn it.

reason.description: Why it is unavailable or invalid.

structural.description: One of the runtime's structural roles (default, explorer, worker, reviewer): not editable, and not overridable.

agent.description: The declarative agent the child was spawned from (`security-reviewer`), when it was; `role` is then only its capability class.

UiAgentProblem.description: Something under an agents directory that is not an agent at all.

UiAgentStatus.description: Whether an entry can be spawned here.

oneOf.description: Valid, and everything it names exists on this machine.
Valid, but something it names is missing here (model, skill, effort).
The definition itself is broken; it cannot be spawned anywhere.

UiApprovalRequest.description: A pending permission request, projected for display.

always_persists.description: Whether "always allow" would persist a standing permission rule for this action. When `false` (consent tools such as `save_agent` or `remember`, actions with no safe rule shape, or a request recorded before this field) the runtime could only honour it for this turn, so a client must not offer it.

call_id.description:
The tool call this request is holding, when the runtime knows it.

A UI needs it to tell "announced, waiting for you" apart from "running": the call has an event on screen already, and without an id the only way to find its row would be to guess at the latest running call. `None` for a request that is not about one specific call (a standing `request_permissions`), and for a session recorded before this field.

command.description: The concrete command, when the tool is `run_command`.

grant.description: Exact host-resolved capability/resource metadata, never inferred from text.

requires_human_consent.description: A human-only consent operation offers Once and Deny exclusively.

risks.description: Human-readable risk bullets (paths touched, network, etc.).

summary.description: A one-line summary of what will happen.

UiBackgroundTaskRecord.description: One background task as the snapshot reconciles it: durable start, durable terminal record, and the live registry, never a fabricated outcome.

call_id.description: The tool call that started the task, when the start was recorded.

duration_ms.description:
How long the task's execution was observed, when a fact establishes it.

A lost task's duration ends at the proven loss, not at the moment a client happens to read the record: work whose owner is gone must not appear to keep growing. Absent when no observed start or end exists.

lifetime.description: The lifetime the spawn promised (`goal`, `runtime`, `session`, `persistent`). Absent on a terminal-only record written before starts were recorded.

output.description: The bounded output tail retained with the terminal fact. Empty when no terminal record exists; a live task's output is still a live event.

UiBackgroundTaskState.description:
The lifecycle state of a background task, as the runtime can establish it from durable facts.

This is deliberately not the process registry's status: a task that the registry no longer holds may have completed, been cancelled, or died with the runtime that hosted it. `Lost` and `Unknown` keep those apart instead of rewriting an absent record as success or failure.

oneOf.description: The live registry still holds the process.
A durable terminal record says it exited zero.
A durable terminal record says it exited non-zero, or exited without a code.
A durable terminal record says it was stopped by a user/agent cancel or session cleanup.
The task started, but the boot that hosted it is gone and no terminal record exists. The process may have died with that runtime; nothing here claims either completion or failure.
No live entry and no terminal record, and the owning boot cannot be proven gone (or the start carries no attribution). State unknown.
Two durable starts share one task id. Neither the live process nor a terminal record can be attributed to one of them safely, so both stay unclassified rather than guessing.

UiCheckpoint.description: A conversation restore point (spec §68). Restoring truncates the transcript back to `ordinal` messages; working-tree files are left to the user's git.

ordinal.description: The persisted-message count to truncate back to.

UiChildAgent.description: One delegated child, projected from the durable record — what a client that reconnects, or opens a session, renders without having seen a single live event.

agent.description: The declarative agent it was spawned from, when it was. `None` for a built-in role spawn and for children recorded before agents existed.

background.description: Whether its parent continued while it ran.

cost_usd_micros.description: `None` when no call carried a price — unknown, not zero.

input_tokens.description: Model usage recorded under this child's id.

limit.description: Which bound fired when `stop` is [`ChildStop::Budget`]. `None` for every other stop and for terminals recorded before it was carried.

ok.description: Whether it reached the end of its task, once settled. Carried beside `outcome` because rows settled before the outcome was typed have only this bit.

purpose.description: What it was asked to do.

resumes.description: How many times it was continued after an interruption.

scope.description: Exclusive write scope fixed at spawn (empty when late-bound or read-only).

summary.description: The recorded settlement summary, once settled.

title.description: The child's short task title, fixed at spawn: its identity, distinct from the full instructions in `purpose`. `None` on children recorded before titles existed; a presentation fallback may project `purpose`.

UiChildAgentIdentity.description: The definition a running or settled child was spawned from, as resolved at spawn. Deleting or editing the definition does not change it.

UiChildContribution.description: Everything the inspector shows for one child.

findings.description: Findings this child produced, in ledger order.

measured.description:
Whether a ledger snapshot was found at all.

`false` means the question could not be answered — no ledger, or the child predates finding adoption. It does NOT mean the child found nothing, and the inspector must not render it that way.

read_only.description: Whether this child held a physically read-only toolset.

UiChildState.description:
What one child contributed, as counts plus its capability contract.

A flat mirror of the runtime's projection rather than the runtime type itself: this crate is the stable wire, so an internal refactor of the ledger must not change what clients parse.

`findings_total` is a count, not a score: it says how much this child reported, never whether any of it mattered. What the parent did about it is in the transcript, where the parent said it. Where a delegated child's lifecycle stands, as the runtime records it.

oneOf.description: An activation is live.
Its activation died with a runtime window; the next turn of the session continues it or settles it as lost.
It has its one terminal.

UiClarificationQuestion.description:
One question of a clarification interaction (spec §35).

A clarification is a set of questions the user answers in one sitting; the client shows them as tabs so only one is on screen at a time. `header` is the short tab label, `question` the full prompt.

allow_other.description: Offer a trailing free-text entry ("其他…") next to the options.

header.description: Short label for the question's tab. Empty means "derive one from `question`" — a display concern the client owns.

max_choices.description: Maximum number of picks for a `multi` question (`None` = the option count).

min_choices.description: Minimum number of picks for a `multi` question (0 = none required).

UiClarificationRequest.description: A mid-task clarification the agent needs answered (spec §35).

options.description: Candidate answers, when the model offered a choice.

question.description: The interaction's headline, and the whole prompt for a request that predates `questions`.

questions.description: The questions to answer in one interaction. Empty for a legacy single-question request: clients then render `question`/`options` as one question, so an older runtime keeps working against a newer client and vice versa.

UiCommandStop.description: How a stopped command call ended, as the runtime established it.

oneOf.description: The whole process tree was confirmed gone.
The tree was signalled, but its termination could not be confirmed.

patch.description: The unified diff hunk text, loaded on demand.

UiEventRelation.description: Identity-based relation (never inferred from wall-clock proximity).

UiExecutionTask.description: The durable task a Chat session owes, as projected for a client that is reconnecting. `objective` is the goal's text, never the session title.

running.description: A live turn is executing it. False means the work is owed but no window is running; the user can resume it.

user_paused.description: The user's own stop directive is still in force: the durable `goals.user_paused_at` column, not a client-side reading of the transcript. A paused goal owes work and withholds it at the same time, which `running` alone cannot express while an unrelated turn runs.

UiFailure.description:
A structured product failure attached to a terminal turn failure.

`detail` is the raw diagnostic and belongs on disclosure only; every other field is machine semantics suitable for choosing an icon, a title, and an action without reading the message.

detail.description: The raw technical detail. Disclosure only — never the primary line.

model.description: The model id the failing request was addressed to, when known.

provider.description: The provider id, when the failure came from a provider call.

provider_code.description: The provider's own error code, when it reported one.

request_id.description: The provider's correlation id for the failing request, when the response exposed one. The single most useful field for a support report against a vendor.

retries.description: Automatic retries the runtime spent before this became terminal. Absent when the failure never went through a retry loop.

status.description: HTTP status, when the failure had one.

summary.description: A short, provider-agnostic one-line product explanation for the primary line (e.g. "模型服务拒绝了当前请求。"). Clients may override it with their own localization keyed on `category`.

UiFinding.description:
One finding, as the inspector shows it.

A projection of `leveler_lifecycle::FindingRecord`, not the record itself: this crate is the stable wire, and the ledger must stay free to change.

id.description: Parent-ledger id (`f-1`). Stable enough for a user to refer to.

UiForeignOrigin.description: The durable source identity of an imported CodeLeveler session.

source_cwd.description: Working directory recorded by the source session, when present.

source_path.description: The exact source file the read-only history tool addresses. The client shows this as provenance; it never rewrites it.

UiForeignSession.description: One locally discovered source session, as a picker needs it.

cwd.description: Working directory recorded by the source session.

native_id.description: The source agent's own session id.

updated_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC, derived from the source file.

UiForeignTool.description: The agent whose local session store is read.

oneOf.description: Anthropic Claude Code.
OpenAI Codex.

workspace_available.description: Availability is separate from lifecycle; a deleted checkout retains its history.

UiGoalRecap.description:
One durable goal checkpoint, projected for history presentation (long-goal P3). Every Recap a client renders maps to exactly one persisted checkpoint (`checkpoint_id`) — the client presents these fields, it never rebuilds its own summary, and it never parses `display_summary` to reconstruct facts.

Truth rules ride the shape: `findings_total == None` means the ledger was not readable when the checkpoint was cut — UNKNOWN, which a client must never render as zero.

created_at.description: RFC3339. When the checkpoint was cut.

display_summary.description: The 1–2 line presentation. Runtime-rendered: the semantic summary when one exists, otherwise the deterministic structured fallback.

plan_completed.description: Plan progress; both `None` when no plan was recorded (absent, not 0/0).

transcript_ordinal.description: Transcript position the checkpoint represents (messages `[0..n)`), so a reopened session can interleave the Recap where it happened. `None` = unknown; append after existing history.

UiHistoryEntry.description: One fact of a past turn, as the live stream carried it.

turn_elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds from the start of the turn this entry belongs to, taken from the durable record times — a replay has no live clock.

turn_start.description: The first entry of a turn.

UiInputState.description: The terminal state of an accepted mid-turn input.

oneOf.description: The input's transcript row is durable and was part of a model request.
The task was cancelled before the input was delivered.

UiInterruptedCallState.description: How much the runtime can prove about an interrupted tool call's owner.

oneOf.description: The runtime that owned the turn is provably gone, so the call is no longer executing here. Its side effect may still have completed, or left an orphaned process; the outcome is unknown either way.
The owning turn still exists, but its runtime cannot be proven dead or alive. The call may still be executing. Never shown as interrupted, completed, or failed.

UiInterruptedToolCall.description:
A tool call that started but never recorded an outcome.

This is the crash window's evidence: a `tool_call_started` without a matching `tool_call_finished`. The next turn is refused until the user acknowledges it, because the call may already have produced its side effect and replaying it would duplicate that effect. The snapshot carries the list so a client that just reconnected can show the problem without first attempting a turn.

pending_approval.description: The call was still waiting for an approval when the runtime died. Its side effect had not started; the user still has to acknowledge that the recovery decision is theirs.

UiLaneAccounting.description: What one lane of a session spent. `lane` is `main`, `children` or `total`.

projected_input_tokens.description: Summed over the lane's rows that recorded a runtime projection estimate; `None` when none did (an unmeasured figure is not a zero).

projected_reasoning_tokens.description: Of the projected input, the historical-reasoning slice the route carried back. A slice of `projected_input_tokens`, not of `reasoning_tokens` (which is output-side). `None` = no projection was recorded.

UiMessage.description: A rendered message in the transcript.

images.description: How many images this message carried. A client renders them its own way — the text never holds a file path, and a message that was only a picture would otherwise read as an empty one. Additive: 0 on old runtimes and on every message that carried none.

kind.description: What kind of message this is when its role alone would mislead. `None` is an ordinary message of its role.

ordinal.description: Persisted transcript ordinal (append order in the message log), when known. Lets a client interleave durable goal recaps at the position their checkpoint represents. Additive: absent on live-stream messages and old runtimes.

UiMessageKind.description: A message whose role does not say who wrote it.

oneOf.description: Written by the runtime into the model's context as a user-role turn — a child's settlement, a lost or resumed delegation — not typed by the user. Render it as a runtime notice, never as user input.
Typed by the user while a turn ran, accepted durably, and not yet in any model request. Joins the running turn at its next round.
Typed by the user while a turn ran, accepted durably, and now part of the transcript and a model request.
Accepted, then settled without delivery because the user cancelled the task. It must stay visible as such and must never run later.

UiModelUsage.description: One provider/model's share of a report. Requests are grouped by the provider key and the model id actually sent on the wire, so switching models mid-session splits here instead of blending.

cached_input_tokens.description: Subset of `input_tokens`; `None` when no row in the group recorded it.

cost_usd_micros.description: Sum over the group's priced rows; `None` when none of them had a price.

priced_requests.description: Rows in the group that carried a price.

reasoning_tokens.description: Subset of `output_tokens`; `None` when no row in the group recorded it.

requests.description: Provider calls in this group, retries included — each is a billed call.

unmeasured_requests.description: Calls in this group whose provider reported no usage at all.

UiObservabilityLoaded.description: Bounded event window + related observation slices. Current and historical sessions use this same payload.

UiObservationField.description: One inspect key/value. Avoids tuple arrays in the JSON schema.

fields.description: Safe inspect fields only (no raw args, no prompt, no secrets).

status.description:
running | ok | fail | unknown | info

`unknown` is a terminal state of its own: the call's outcome could not be established after a crash. It is neither success, failure, nor a still-running call, and must not be collapsed into any of them.

UiPendingInteraction.description: A live control request included in a reconnect snapshot. Only requests with an in-process waiter are projected; interrupted turns never resurrect stale buttons after a process restart.

state.description: Lifecycle of the newest declaration. Older runtimes omit it, which decodes as [`UiPlanState::Active`] — their only previous behavior.

UiPlanState.description:
Whether the plan is the current turn's work or durable history.

The durable log keeps every declaration; this field is the runtime's authoritative classification of the newest one. A plan from before a task terminal is still returned after a restart, but never as active work.

oneOf.description: The newest declaration belongs to an epoch with no task terminal.
The owning task finished normally.
The owning task failed, was cancelled, or its process died.

UiPlanStep.description: One step in the execution plan.

UiRecoveryObservation.description: Recovery facts that are already durable and safe to show.

agent_id.description: The sub-agent that made the call; absent for the root session's own.

error_detail.description: What the transport observed of a response whose body could not be read, as JSON. Diagnostic: it distinguishes a damaged answer from no answer.

projected_input_tokens.description: What the runtime projected this call's prompt would cost, priced over the provider-visible request. Beside `input_tokens`, never instead of it — the pair is what makes an estimate error readable. `None` = no projection was recorded for this call.

projected_reasoning_tokens.description: Of that projected input, the historical-reasoning slice the wire carried. A slice of `projected_input_tokens`; `None` = not recorded.

reasoning_tokens.description: Subset of `output_tokens` spent on reasoning, when the provider reported a breakdown. `None` = not reported.

UiSessionHistory.description: The existing bounded history projection, captured with an in-flight snapshot so a reconnect preserves completed members and real group boundaries.

UiSessionObservation.description: Session-level observation header + aggregates from durable stores.

cached_input_tokens.description: Prompt tokens the provider served from cache — a SUBSET of `input_tokens`. `None` when no request recorded the figure at all; that is an absence of measurement, and summing it as zero would report a cache miss nobody observed.

cost_usd_micros.description: Summed over the requests that carry a price. `None` when none does.

duration_ms.description: Wall clock from the session's first to its latest durable timestamp. `None` when either end is unparseable.

lanes.description: Spend split by who did it: the root session, its children, and the total. Present whenever there is a request to attribute.

reasoning_tokens.description: Reasoning tokens summed over the requests that reported a breakdown — a SUBSET of `output_tokens`, never an addition to it. `None` when no request reported one, which is an absence of measurement.

work_profile.description: Deprecated compatibility marker, always `single` on new runtimes.

UiSessionSnapshot.description: Everything a client needs to render a session's header and transcript.

active_background_tasks.description: Registry-backed background processes still active for this session. Additive/defaulted so older runtimes decode as no known live process.

active_tools.description: Live render state needed to reconnect while a long turn is still running. All fields are additive/defaulted for protocol compatibility.

available_models.description: Models the user can switch to (for the model picker, ).

background_tasks.description: Every background task the durable log knows for this session, including the ones the live registry no longer holds. A task that vanished with a crashed runtime appears as `lost`, never as completed and never as a silently dropped record. Additive: an older runtime reports none.

branch.description: VCS branch, if the repository is a git repo.

children.description: Every delegated child of this session, oldest first, from durable storage.

collaboration.description: Product collaboration axis (`chat | plan | goal`). The runtime routes submissions and applies the read-only planning overlay from this value.

execution_task.description: A durable task committed from a Chat turn that still owes work. Additive: absent when no goal is running. The session's collaboration axis says the interaction mode, not whether work is owed.

finalization_stage.description: Typed in-flight terminalization stage. Present only while the runtime still owns an active turn after the final assistant message.

foreign_origin.description: Where this session came from when it was created by importing another agent's session. Additive: absent on an ordinary native session and on runtimes that predate import.

interrupted_tool_calls.description: Tool calls whose outcome a crash left unknown. Non-empty means the next turn is blocked behind the crash-recovery gate until the user acknowledges it; nothing is replayed by that acknowledgement. Additive: an older runtime reports none.

last_sequence.description: The event-log sequence this snapshot reflects — the resync anchor. A client that fell behind (broadcast lag, reconnect) takes a fresh snapshot and resumes the event stream *after* this sequence, so it neither double-applies nor misses a canonical event. `None` when unknown (e.g. a brand-new session with no events yet).

latest_turn_ordinal.description: Ordinal of the newest durable turn in this session. A client that submitted work and later correlates its terminal compares this value: the projected terminal always belongs to the newest turn, so an ordinal that moved on means a different turn now owns the terminal. Additive: an older runtime reports `None`.

recaps.description: Durable goal recaps for this session's goals (long-goal P3), oldest first. Each maps to one persisted GoalCheckpoint; a reopened client interleaves them into history by `transcript_ordinal`. Additive.

thinking.description: Runtime-projected Thinking Level state, in the user's own vocabulary. Absent on old runtimes so a new client keeps its boot-time value; a present value with `access: unsupported` means the model cannot be asked, which the client says rather than inventing a level.

user_shells.description: User shell executions: the active one (if any) plus a bounded recent history, newest last. Additive/defaulted like the rest of this block.

vision.description: Whether the current model accepts image input (spec §42).

work_profile.description: Deprecated compatibility field. New runtimes emit `single`; historical values never control tool exposure. Clients must not display a selector.

UiSessionSummary.description: A one-line session summary for the Sessions screen (spec §52).

declaration.description: Latest durable task declaration; absent for legacy or non-declaration endings.

repository.description: Repository root the session belongs to. Filled by the runtime that owns the session and by the WebUI aggregation router (multi-project grouping); omitted on the wire when unknown so old fixtures and clients keep parsing.

UiShadowedAgent.description: A lower-precedence definition the active one hides.

UiTaskDeclaration.description: A task's own terminal declaration, projected from its durable TaskFinished stop. This is not verification evidence and does not replace session lifecycle.

UiTaskTerminal.description: Latest committed TaskFinished fact. This does not prove a later turn settled.

UiThinkingAccess.description: How a model's thinking can be controlled.

oneOf.description: The model does not reason.
The model reasons, but nobody can ask for a different amount.
The caller can choose a level.

UiThinkingState.description:
The session's Thinking Level, in CodeLeveler's own vocabulary.

Every field is a canonical level (`auto`, `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `max`). A client renders these and offers `choices`; it must not derive a level from a model name, from a provider's parameter, or from any other field on the wire — the runtime is the only place that knows what a level means for a model, and it answers here in the user's words.

access.description: Whether this model's thinking can be controlled at all.

choices.description: The levels worth offering on this model: one entry per level that actually differs, `auto` first. Empty when `access` is not adjustable.

configured.description: The configured level for this model: its own `[models.<id>] thinking`, else the global `thinking`.

current.description: What the user asked for: `session_override` when set, else `configured`.

effective.description:
What is actually in effect for this model right now.

Equal to `current` when this model can express it. Otherwise `auto`: the request carries no reasoning override at all, and the provider's own default applies. A client that showed `current` as if it were running would be reporting a setting that is not in use.

session_override.description: The session's explicit override. `None` means the session inherits `configured` — which is not the same as `Some(Auto)`.

UiToolAggregate.description: Per-tool aggregate for the **whole session**, independent of the event window. Paired on `(call_id, agent_id)`; duration only from a matching start+finish. Unfinished starts are not success and do not invent duration.

failed.description:
Finished with `is_error = true` and a reported result.

A call whose outcome the crash window left unknown — even when the raw finish row carries `is_error = true` because the client had to fill in a shape — is counted in [`Self::unknown`], not here.

unknown.description: Finished with an outcome that could not be established (crash-window acknowledgement marker). Unknown is not failure and not success.

UiToolTiming.description: One tool's timing on a shared, turn-local runtime timeline. Live sources and replay sources use the same persisted monotonic execution facts. Wall-clock timestamps never stand in for missing execution boundaries. Absence means unknown, never an assumed zero. The start coordinate lets clients measure overlapping calls as a span instead of adding durations.

clock_id.description: Only coordinates with this exact clock identity can form one span.

UiTurnUsage.description:
One finished turn's provider usage, projected from the runtime's durable `model_requests` rows.

This is a settled fact, not a running sum of streamed snapshots: re-reading it after a reconnect, a resume or a replay yields the same figures. `unmeasured_requests` keeps a call whose provider reported no usage distinguishable from a measured zero.
